Riley: heads-up from onboarding pegasus-31k (int3). Repro shows deterministic token shift when multi-host prefill interleaves across shard boundaries. float32/int16 baselines clean.
Samir: can you share the exact repro and quant tag?
Riley: branch feature/quant-onboard, quant artifact q-int3-v1. repro: `./run/long_prefill --model pegasus-31k --quant int3 --context 42000 --shards 4 --prefill-interleave=host` plus `--seed 1337`.
Juno: "prefill-interleave=host"? that's the new optimization that sends alternating prefill chunks to hosts to parallelize IO, right?
Riley: yup. observed pattern: fingerprints identical to baseline until ~32768 then tokens align shifted by one after a host boundary. logs show duplicate kv keys with different absolute_pos attached. snippet:
```
[20:04:01] host0 prefill chunk start abs_pos=32760 len=64 chunk_id=0x1a
[20:04:01] host1 prefill chunk start abs_pos=32760 len=64 chunk_id=0x1b
[20:04:02] kv: write key=0x7f3d abs_pos=32762 src=host0
[20:04:02] kv: write key=0x7f3d abs_pos=32762 src=host1
[20:04:03] token-check expected=token_32765 actual=token_32764
```
Samir: that looks like collision due to identical key derivation when two hosts encode identical relative positions independently. How are keys salted per-host?
Riley: current design salts by request-id only; when interleaving we reuse request-id for the prefill session and per-host offsets are applied separately, causing identical derived key for two different host-relative writes.
Kai: interesting. workaround would be to include host-id in the key salt or make request-id incorporate host-shard mapping. Before patching, can you run with `--prefill-interleave=none` and `--kv-debug=full` to confirm?
Riley: did that. with interleave=none no drift. with interleave=host and kv-debug we see same key double-writes. added quick local patch to salt with host id and the drift disappears in smoke.
Juno: does int3 quant change the encoding behavior? i.e., different chunking/tiling could change exact timing and exacerbate the overlap?
Riley: int3 kernel packs tokens tighter so more frequent prefill chunk boundaries -> increases chance of concurrent writes to same nominal abs_pos. float32 baseline had larger chunking which hid it.
Samir: plan: 1) add host-id to key-salt for prefill writes 2) add invariant assert in prefill handshake: if key exists and absolute_pos != incoming_abs_pos then log full conflict and skip stale write 3) run matrix: prefill-interleave {host, none}, quant {float16, int3, int4}, shards {1,4} 4) canary on dedicated pool.
Riley: will open PR for host-salt + handshake assert and run small matrix. uploading artifacts to s3://redwood-eval/pegasus_prefill/1931234567.tar.gz
eval-bot: longprefill-eval queued (job id: lp-123900). baseline float16 pass. int3 interleave=host reproduces 5/5.
Kai: ops note 1 1  can we get 3xA100 for a 90m canary? cc ops.
Samir: also add `--kv-dump=compact` to repro script so we can diff key lists quickly. If host-salt patch fixes it, we'll include as hotfix for onboarding models and add migration to reconcile already-written keys.
Juno: good catch. this is a nice example of a correctness bug triggered by newer optimization (interleaving) + tighter quant packing. makes sense.
Riley: filing INF-1722 to track. will post PR and matrix results here. :rocket:
